questions.q: What is "distillation" in the context of building an SFT dataset?
options: Removing noisy tokens from the tokenizer vocabulary
Using a stronger existing model to generate training responses to a set of instructions, which scales more cheaply than pure human authorship
Compressing a trained model's weights to 4-bit precision
A technique for packing multiple conversations into one sequence
questions.explain: Distillation for SFT data means generating responses with an existing capable model rather than having humans write every response, making large-scale dataset creation far cheaper.

questions.q: In the standard prompt-masking implementation, what value are label positions for prompt tokens typically set to, and why?
options: 0, because zero means 'low priority' to the loss function
-100, a sentinel value that PyTorch's CrossEntropyLoss (and Hugging Face trainer internals) treats as 'ignore this position'
1, to give prompt tokens full weight equal to response tokens
The vocabulary size, to force an error if accidentally used
questions.explain: By convention, prompt-token label positions are set to -100, a sentinel that CrossEntropyLoss is configured to ignore, excluding those positions from the loss calculation.

questions.q: In a multi-turn conversation, which assistant turns should be unmasked (contribute to the loss)?
options: Only the final assistant turn
Every assistant turn across the whole conversation, not just the last one
Only the first assistant turn
No assistant turns should ever be masked out
questions.explain: The masking principle applies to every assistant turn in a multi-turn conversation. Unmasking only the last turn would silently discard most of the training signal from earlier turns.

questions.q: Why is packing multiple conversations into one training sequence riskier for SFT than it is for pretraining?
options: Packing is not supported at all by TRL's SFTTrainer
Without attention masking or position-id resets to prevent cross-conversation attention, the model risks learning to treat one conversation's end as a cue to start an unrelated new one
Packing always produces worse tokenization for instruction data
Packing only works with human-written data, never distilled data
questions.explain: Unlike pretraining documents where boundaries mostly don't matter, packed SFT conversations risk cross-conversation bleed-through unless attention is explicitly blocked between the packed examples.

questions.q: What does TRL's `SFTTrainer` handle internally when given a dataset in the standard conversational `messages` format?
options: Nothing -- the user must manually apply the chat template and build label masks before passing data in
Chat-template application and prompt masking, which is why it's the practical default over hand-rolling that logic
Only the learning-rate schedule, with no data formatting support
Converting the model from fp32 to fp16 automatically
questions.explain: SFTTrainer applies the tokenizer's chat template and handles prompt masking internally for conversational-format datasets, which is why it's preferred over manually implementing that logic.
